pending_commit.commit_message: CHROMIUM: bluetooth/sco - Parse correct conn handle According to Core spec 5.4.3 HCI Synchronous Data Packets the Connection_Handle uses the first 12 bits of header. This change fixes the connection handle value. Otherwise if the succeeding 2 bits of packet status flag is set, it could result in connection look up failure and drop one SCO packet. BUG=chromium:980454 TEST=Test wideband speech headset, verify there's no error printed for 'SCO packet for unknown connection handle' Change-Id: Idab09b69de768fc4113476409c9435af730dae7b Signed-off-by: Hsin-Yu Chao <hychao@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1718627 Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: bluetooth/sco - Keep HCI SCO packet header in transparent mode According to Core spec 5.4.3 HCI Synchronous Data Packets, when erroneous data reporting feature is enabled, controller sets the packet status flag to indicate if data is intact in the payload. For wide band speech mode using voice_transparent settings, user space wants to know the value of packet status flag for packet loss concealment. We shall not strip the HCI SCO packet header in this case. BUG=chromium:980454 TEST=Apply CRAS patches and test WBS headset. Verified the erroneous data reporting is working fine by flagging lost/partial data. Change-Id: If90925f605e5f67a2815bea4a875b3d05359a758 Signed-off-by: Hsin-Yu Chao <hychao@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1718628 Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: bluetooth/sco - Check for NULL socket in receiving sco data When recv_scodata is called, the hci_conn may actually hold a NULL sock hence accessing the settings of sco_pinfo causes crash. Fix this by moving the hci_conn socket NULL check earlier, to make sure we access valid sco_pinfo settings before taking care of HCI SCO header and call to sco_recv_frame. BUG=chromium:980454 TEST=Repeatedly stress wideband speech with BT headset, verify kernel doesn't crash. Change-Id: Ibe91a46964919507c2c8db2788567a86ce600819 Signed-off-by: Hsin-Yu Chao <hychao@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1718629 Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: drm/i915: Disable boost and waitboost The GT frequency should ideally scale as per the load, but on making a Hangouts call or opening the camera preview it is pegged to max frequency. This leads to higher than expected power consumption(2W+). The camera stack is probably doing some heavy handed sync operations which causes the GPU to be always stuck at max frequency. This is a temporary fix until the userspace(camera) is either fixed or optimized because we may incur a performance penalty due to this change. This bug is discussed here[1]. 1. https://bugs.freedesktop.org/show_bug.cgi?id=110750 BUG=b:130638275, b:131723850 TEST=Build and boot on nocturne. Make sure GPU frequency is low when running camera app. Change-Id: I662fada3093ccd5a3424b90dca48deb176a9c313 Signed-off-by: Ricky Liang <jcliang@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1657492 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org>
